title: Bank of England Freezes $1.95 Billion Venezuelan Gold Reserves
reason: Multiple independent sources confirm: in Nov-Dec 2018 Venezuela's central bank (BCV) requested withdrawal of its gold from the Bank of England, and following the UK government's Feb 4, 2019 recognition of Juan Guaidó as interim president, the BoE refused to honor withdrawal instructions from the Maduro-appointed BCV board. The gold total was ~31 tonnes (after a Dec 2018 Deutsche Bank swap closeout raised holdings from 14 to 31 tonnes). UK Supreme Court documents value the reserves at approximately $1.95 billion (as of 2020 court filings; the exact USD figure fluctuates with gold price over time, with other snapshots giving $1.2-1.8bn). A multi-year legal dispute followed (Maduro-appointed board sued the BoE in 2020; courts including the UK Supreme Court in 2021 ruled based on the 'one voice' recognition doctrine, generally favoring the UK-recognized side; the dispute continued into 2023 and beyond as the UK's recognition of Guaidó itself lapsed). This matches the event description in country, year, and substance (magnitude, actors, and outcome all check out).

title: Regional Elections — Opposition Wins Several Governorships
reason: Core event confirmed: Venezuela held regional elections on 21 November 2021; PSUV won the large majority of governorships (widely reported as ~18-20 of 23) while the opposition made symbolically significant gains, including Cojedes and Nueva Esparta (Fuerza Vecinal's Morel Rodríguez beat PSUV 43-39%), Zulia (Manuel Rosales beat incumbent PSUV governor 57-37%), and — after a contested rerun on 9 January 2022 — Barinas, Chávez's home state, won by opposition candidate Sergio Garrido (55.4%) over PSUV's Jorge Arreaza. However, the description's inclusion of Anzoátegui as an opposition win is factually backwards: PSUV's Luis Marcano won Anzoátegui with ~46% of the vote, unseating the sitting opposition governor Antonio Barreto Sira (who placed third) — i.e., PSUV flipped that state FROM the opposition, not the reverse. Multiple sources confirm PSUV "overturned rightwing incumbents in Mérida, Táchira and Anzoátegui." The real headline opposition win omitted from the description is Zulia, Venezuela's most populous state. So year/country/overall thrust hold, but one of the four named governorships (Anzoátegui) is a materially wrong actor/scope detail.
